headroom.label: Headroom — the inverse question
headroom.formula: floor((envelope - base_forecast) / slice_base) as a percent of the slice
headroom.sentence: {room}{unit} more on {driver} before the base case crosses the envelope.
headroom.help: Goal-Seek-style and exact — the inverse of the decomposition, not a forecast.

worked_example.question: How far can the overhaul price index rise before the base case crosses the PPI envelope?
worked_example.solved_from: envelope 34.5M − base forecast 33.0M = 1.5M of headroom ÷ the 14.4M index-linked slice
worked_example.note: Goal-Seek-style and exact — the inverse of the decomposition, not a forecast.

runtime.closing_note: A lever moves only the slice the graph can attribute to that driver. Locked slices and the unattributed residual never move — smearing an unattributed amount across drivers would invent a sensitivity the data does not have.

publishing.call: The scenario — the frame (watched measures, exposed drivers and their ranges) plus its cases. A case is never published on its own.

readers.label: Readers
readers.caveat: This narrows who is told the scenario exists. It is not access control.
readers.scope_note: Publishing never widens access. Each reader opens the scenario under their own data-access rules; a masked measure stays masked.

graph.label: Bind to a graph
graph.note: A published scenario points to one published graph version and re-traverses it on every open. When a newer graph is published the author can re-bind.
graph.empty: Nothing is published, so there is no graph to bind a scenario to.
